items.name: HL · Morning weather → Sheet
items.what: Every morning at 06:30 Lagos time, fetches Ibadan's forecast from Open-Meteo, shapes it into one row with rider advice, and appends it to the HL Weather sheet.
setup: Start n8n in Docker with a volume and your timezone: run docker volume create n8n_data, then docker run -it --name n8n -p 5678:5678 -e GENERIC_TIMEZONE="Africa/Lagos" -e TZ="Africa/Lagos" -e N8N_ENFORCE_SETTINGS_FILE_PERMISSIONS=true -e N8N_RUNNERS_ENABLED=true -v n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n n8nio/n8n (or open an n8n Cloud trial instead).
Open http://localhost:5678 and create the owner account with a strong password.
Create a Google Sheet called HL Weather whose first tab (Sheet1) has the headers date, max_temp_c, rain_chance, rain_mm, advice in row 1.

Create a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential called "Google Sheets" (Cloud: sign in with Google; self-hosted: create an OAuth client in Google Cloud Console and paste n8n's OAuth Redirect URL exactly). Select it in the Google Sheets node.
Replace YOUR_SHEET_ID in the Google Sheets node with your HL Weather sheet's ID (the long string in its URL). If your tab isn't called Sheet1, pick it from the list.
Save, then Publish the workflow so the 06:30 schedule runs on its own.
items.test: Click Execute workflow: the HTTP Request output shows daily lists such as temperature_2m_max: [30.4], Edit Fields shows one item with five fields (numbers without brackets), and one row lands in HL Weather. After publishing, Executions should show a run you didn't start at 06:30 the next morning.

walk.title: Build it: the morning weather log
walk.sample: Ibadan forecast for 2026-10-05 · max 30.4 °C · rain chance 78% · 5.3 mm

steps.say: Start n8n in Docker with a volume and the Lagos timezone. The volume keeps your workflows and credentials when the container restarts, and the timezone makes six thirty mean six thirty in Ibadan.
Our trigger is a schedule: every day at six thirty in the morning, before the riders head out.
Next, an HTTP Request to Open-Meteo for Ibadan's forecast. It needs no key, so there's no credential here.
Click Execute step and read the JSON. Notice each daily value is a list, even with one day of forecast.
Edit Fields shapes one tidy item. We use square bracket zero to take the number out of each list, and every value is set to Expression, not Fixed.
The advice field turns the numbers into something a rider can act on. Sixty percent or more means pack tarpaulins and start early.
show: ? "Rain likely: pack tarpaulins, start deliveries early"

steps.say: Set the number fields' type to Number, so the sheet can chart and sum them later.
Finally, append the row to the HL Weather sheet. The Google login lives in a credential, never typed into a field.
Mapping is set to Map Automatically. Because our field names match the headers exactly, every column fills itself.
show: Headers: date · max_temp_c · rain_chance · rain_mm · advice

steps.say: Execute the workflow once, then Save and Publish. Saving alone never runs on a schedule. One run a day is about thirty executions a month, however many nodes it has.

walk.end: Execute the workflow, check the new row, then publish it and look in Executions tomorrow for a run you didn't start.
